create.name: FPMT (Foundation for the Preservation of the Mahayana Tradition)
create.bio:
FPMT is an international Tibetan Buddhist network founded by two Gelug lamas, Lama Yeshe and his student Lama Zopa Rinpoche, whose teaching follows the line of the fourteenth-century master Lama Tsongkhapa. Its centres, study groups and retreat places around the world share a common set of study programmes, and an international office in Portland, Oregon, writes the curricula, prepares prayer and practice texts, trains teachers and supports the affiliated centres.

Study runs from introductory meditation and mindfulness courses through Discovering Buddhism and Living in the Path to the five-year Basic Program and the longer Masters Program, much of it also open online through the FPMT Online Learning Center. The YouTube channel, running since 2007, holds full-length teachings, short extracts and clips of Lama Zopa Rinpoche, including long recorded retreats, alongside interviews with senior monks and teachers and news of the organisation's charitable work. A podcast, the Essential Extracts, offers shorter excerpts from Lama Zopa Rinpoche on single lamrim topics, and the organisation also publishes Mandala magazine.

courses.title: Discovering Buddhism
courses.description: A foundation course in Tibetan Buddhist thought and meditation, taught at FPMT centres or studied online in modules that combine video, audio, reading and short retreats.

courses.title: Living in the Path
courses.description: An online programme built from video excerpts and edited transcripts of Lama Zopa Rinpoche's teachings, arranged by topic, with a forum for questions to a facilitator.

courses.title: FPMT Basic Program
courses.description: A five-year study course in twelve subjects designed by Lama Zopa Rinpoche, working through classic texts of sutra and tantra for committed students, at centres or online.

free_resources.title: Essential Extracts podcast
free_resources.description: A free podcast of excerpts from Lama Zopa Rinpoche's longer teachings, each episode about fifteen to thirty minutes on one topic from the stages of the path.
